admin.privacy.guidanceBody: Your end users’ personal data stays under your control. Sanvi processes it on your instructions as a processor or service provider — it never sells or shares it, and it answers your end users’ requests only through you or through the storefront privacy centre acting on your behalf.
admin.privacy.guidanceDetail: As the controller (or business) for your end users’ data, you are responsible for answering their requests within the deadline of the jurisdiction that applies. Use this console to track those deadlines, extend once where the law allows, and record refusals with a reason. Requests submitted here are filed with requester type "tenant operator" so the audit trail distinguishes them from requests your end users filed themselves.

admin.advertising.dashboard.breakdown.ca: Campaign performance for the selected range, per currency
Every revenue figure on this dashboard exists twice: once as the ad platform reports it, once as Sanvi observes it. They appear side by side, each labelled where it is shown, and they are never merged into one number.
A single blended figure would be a confident lie: attribution windows differ, so the two numbers legitimately differ.
Conversion value (platform) — the platform's own attribution
Counted by {platform}'s own attribution model, inside the conversion window configured on that platform's account.
Revenue (Sanvi) — observed in your own orders
Revenue from Sanvi's own order records, matched to ad clicks where a click id exists. It follows your checkout, not the platform's model.

The two numbers answer different questions. The platform's number measures what its model credits to your ads; Sanvi's number measures revenue your orders actually recorded. Neither is wrong, and neither is a subset of the other.
Recent days are still inside the platforms' restatement windows: platforms revise freshly reported days as more data arrives, so those numbers may still change.

admin.advertising.tracking.title: Conversion tracking
admin.advertising.tracking.description: What the storefront records when an order is paid, and where each event is sent.
admin.advertising.tracking.disabledBody: The storefront beacon is not emitted while tracking is off, and events are not queued for later — they are lost for the duration. Nothing is uploaded and nothing is captured until tracking is enabled again.
admin.advertising.tracking.captureBody: When an order is paid, the storefront fires one {event} event to this store's own domain. The event carries the order's value and reference. Capturing an event and uploading it to an ad platform are different things — upload is decided per event by the privacy directives below.
admin.advertising.tracking.matrixDescrip: One storefront event can map to a different conversion action per platform. Each action id comes from the platform's own conversion settings — an empty cell means the event is not sent to that platform.
admin.advertising.tracking.saveError: Saving the mappings failed. Try again.
admin.advertising.tracking.emptyMappings: Add an event name below to choose which platform conversion action it maps to.
admin.advertising.tracking.noPlatformsBo: Connect an ad platform first — the matrix columns come from your platforms.
admin.advertising.tracking.consentBody: Every conversion is captured, but uploaded to ad platforms only while measurement is permitted. Without {adsMeasurement}, or with a US opt-out of {saleOrShare} — including one expressed via Global Privacy Control (GPC) — the event is captured but never uploaded. When a mapped platform is a third party, {targetedAdvertising} is asked as well.
admin.advertising.tracking.testDescripti: Sends one synthetic event through the same capture pipeline as the storefront beacon — including the privacy gate — without recording anything. Use it to see what would be captured and what the resolver decides.
admin.advertising.tracking.testError: The test event failed. Try again.
admin.advertising.tracking.resultDecisio: Upload permitted — no directive suppresses this event.

admin.advertising.diagnostics.title: Conversion diagnostics
admin.advertising.diagnostics.descriptio: Why each captured conversion uploaded, stalled, or was never sent — and which causes need action versus respect.
admin.advertising.diagnostics.pausedBody: With tracking paused, the upload workers stop and events wait in the queue — nothing is deleted. Everything already captured is retained and listed below, and uploads resume from the oldest pending event when tracking is enabled again.
admin.advertising.diagnostics.caption: Recent conversions with their upload story
admin.advertising.diagnostics.emptyFilte: Choose another outcome, or clear the filter to see every captured conversion.
admin.advertising.diagnostics.category.m: Ad measurement had not been permitted by this visitor when the event was captured, so nothing was uploaded to any platform.
Nothing to fix — the privacy directive is working as agreed. Uploads start automatically for visitors who allow measurement.
admin.advertising.diagnostics.category.o: This visitor opted out of the sale or sharing of their personal information, so the event was captured but never sent to an ad platform.
Nothing to fix — an opt-out must be honoured, and this one was. The event is never uploaded while the opt-out stands.
admin.advertising.diagnostics.category.b: The visitor's browser sent a privacy signal, and that signal suppresses advertising measurement for the event.
Nothing to fix — a browser signal is binding. Uploads resume automatically for visits that do not carry the signal.
admin.advertising.diagnostics.category.w: The visitor withdrew consent after the event was captured, so the conversion is suppressed and is being removed from any platform that already received it.
Nothing to fix — the withdrawal is honoured and removal is automatic. This event can never be re-sent.
admin.advertising.diagnostics.category.m: No platform click identifier arrived with the event, so the platform cannot attribute it to an ad click and refuses the upload.
Check that your ad links carry their click identifiers through to the storefront. Once a link is fixed, future events attach the id; this event cannot be retrofitted.
admin.advertising.diagnostics.category.t: The platform connection's authorization has lapsed, so uploads to this platform are failing.
Reconnect the platform on the connections screen. Uploads resume automatically from the oldest still-pending event.
admin.advertising.diagnostics.category.u: The platform reported an error while this conversion was being uploaded, or the event exhausted its automatic attempts.
If the event is parked, retry it once the cause is fixed. If errors persist, check the platform's connection health.
admin.advertising.diagnostics.banner.int: Figures cover the conversions currently listed below.
admin.advertising.diagnostics.banner.sup: Suppressed by a privacy directive: {consentAbsent} without measurement consent, {optedOut} opted out of sale/share, {browserSignal} browser privacy signal. These are the privacy system working — not a fault.
admin.advertising.diagnostics.banner.fai: {failing} of {attempted} events with an attempted upload currently have a platform failing or parked. These need action.
admin.advertising.diagnostics.detail.ide: A duplicate storefront beacon resolves to this same event — the identifiers above are what the pipeline deduplicates on.
admin.advertising.diagnostics.detail.cli: None present — platforms cannot attribute a conversion without one.
admin.advertising.diagnostics.detail.noP: No platform uploads were mapped for this event, so nothing has been attempted yet.
admin.advertising.diagnostics.detail.unp: The visitor withdrew consent after the event was captured, but this platform does not support automatic removal, so the conversion may still exist there. Platform reported: {reason}
